post_title: What will the Ibovespa close at on 26 November 2026?

question.title: What will the Ibovespa close at on 26 November 2026?
question.description:
The Ibovespa is the main benchmark index of B3 (Brasil, Bolsa, Balcão), the São Paulo stock exchange, and tracks the most heavily traded stocks on its cash market (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ibovespa).

As of 13 November 2026 the index has just been through one of its most violent repricings in years. It closed at 205,082.56 on 23 October 2026, the last session before the presidential runoff, in which President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) defeated Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) by 51.79% to 48.21%. The market reaction was severe: the index fell 13.88% on 26 October (a circuit breaker was triggered) and lost 18.12% over that week, its worst weekly performance since March 2020. From the 30 October close of 167,921.80 it rebounded to 172,236.05 on 9 November, then closed at 171,336.99 on 10 November, 172,060.43 on 11 November, 171,324.31 on 12 November and 172,013.72 on 13 November — still roughly 16% below its pre-runoff level.

The dominant domestic driver is fiscal policy. On 12 November the Senate approved the base text of the government's fiscal adjustment package (PLP 299/2026) by 45 votes to 31, with an estimated 2027 impact of R$45-56 billion; votes on separate points were postponed to 17 November, and the bill still has to pass the Chamber of Deputies. The real closed at R$5.65/USD on 12 November, its weakest level since June 2025. October IPCA inflation came in at +0.14% month-on-month and +4.63% year-on-year; the Copom's next decision is on 9 December 2026, with Dec/26 DI futures around 13.65%. Abroad, a hotter-than-expected US inflation reading on 10 November pushed up US rate expectations and weighed on emerging-market assets.

Daily moves have recently ranged from about 0.4% to 2.2%, and post-election volatility remains elevated, so a move of several percent over the eight sessions between 13 and 26 November would not be unusual. Thursday 26 November 2026 is a regular B3 trading session (B3's 2026 calendar lists 2 and 20 November as its November market holidays), but US markets are closed for Thanksgiving that day, so Wall Street guidance and foreign flows will be thin. The Yahoo Finance ^BVSP historical data page lists daily open/high/low/close for the index; the row for 26 November 2026 becomes available after the 18:00 BRT close.

question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves to the closing level of the Ibovespa (B3's benchmark index, ticker ^BVSP) for the trading session of Thursday, 26 November 2026, in index points, taken from the 'Close' column of the row dated Nov 26, 2026 in the Yahoo Finance historical prices table at https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/%5EBVSP/history/ (use 'Close', not 'Adj Close'). Values are entered in index points, e.g. a reported close of 173,845.55 points is entered as 173845.55. If that table does not yet show the 26 November 2026 value when checked, resolution waits until it does. If the Yahoo Finance page is unavailable or has no row for that session, the closing level reported for that date by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) will be used.
question.fine_print: A shortened session, trading halt or circuit breaker on 26 November 2026 does not affect resolution; the closing value reported for that session is used as described above.
